description: Team Orbital Sweepers is a one-person team creating. Project Kessler-The Orbital Sweep for Space Mission Design Game Challenge
summary:
Project Kessler : The Orbital Sweep is an interactive arcade-style game designed to raise awareness about orbital congestion and the critical threat of the Kessler Syndrome. Developed as a solo project, the game puts players in control of a specialized cleanup rocket tasked with clearing defunct spacecraft and dangerous debris from Low Earth Orbit.

It addresses the NASA Space Apps challenge by translating complex aerospace science into an engaging, accessible digital experience. By gamifying active debris removal, the project educates players on orbital sustainability while showcasing hand-drawn conceptual artwork to emphasize the urgency of protecting Earth's orbital environment.
details: Project Kessler : The Orbital Sweep is an action-packed arcade-style game where players control an advanced orbital cleanup rocket. The goal is to clear dangerous space debris and defunct satellites from Earth's orbit while avoiding collisions, demonstrating the mechanics of mitigating the Kessler Syndrome in real-time. The project serves as an interactive educational tool. Its primary impact is to raise awareness about the growing crisis of space debris (Kessler Syndrome) in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts to think about orbital sustainability and active debris removal technologies. This project was developed entirely as a solo effort. For the game development, I utilized game-making tools to build a responsive web/playable build. For the visual identity and concept art, I created custom digital illustrations using Procreate on an iPad to design the project's official poster and visual branding. The project creatively combines fast-paced arcade gameplay with real-world orbital mechanics. Instead of a dry scientific report, it translates a complex aerospace engineering problem into an engaging, accessible, and visually striking interactive experience designed entirely within a tight hackathon timeframe. Working as a solo developer, I carefully considered time management, core mechanics prioritization, and visual communication. I focused heavily on core gameplay loops that are fun and intuitive, paired with hand-drawn conceptual artwork that captures the urgency and beauty of protecting Earth's orbit.
dataRefs: The amount of debris in low Earth orbit (LEO) has increased rapidly over the last twenty years, threatening vital satellites. The prevalence of space debris increases the likelihood of cascading collisions, creating debris belts that render many orbits effectively unusable. This cascading effect, in which debris generation outstrips debris re-entry, is known as Kessler Syndrome and some models indicate that it is happening now.

Earth orbital debris issues and recommended future activities are discussed. The workshop addressed the areas of environment definition, hazards to spacecraft, and space object management. It concluded that orbital debris is a potential problem for future space operations. However, before recommending any major efforts to control the environment, more data are required. The most significant required data are on the population of debris smaller than 4 cm in diameter. New damage criteria are also required. When these data are obtained, they can be combined with hypervelocity data to evaluate the hazards to future spacecraft. After these hazards are understood, then techniques to control the environment can be evaluated.
